newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat up on domestic picture, options cited.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat up on domestic picture, options cited.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures were higher at midsession on tight domestic stocks to meet demand from millers plus technical gains, traders said.
"That's all it is (tight stocks) plus technicals," said Skip Searcy of FIMAT Futures.
The March contract was firm relative to other months on options-related buying.
"There was call buying in options. Also locals are short March volatility so any rally could create an even bigger rally," a wheat options specialist said.
Traders said the call buying was short covering.

One firm was central to the options play. FIMAT Futures had purchased 400 March $3.90 calls and "probably will buy up to 1,000 today," a trader said. FIMAT Thursday was said to have purchased 1,000 March $3.90 calls.
The gains in wheat were posted despite stiff competition for the wheat export business.
There was talk Bulgaria bought 300,000 tonnes of wheat from Argentina, that Morocco bought 50,000 from Argentina and ideas Pakistan will buy Australian rather than U.S. wheat.
At 1142 CST, wheat was 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 1/2 lower, with December up 3-1/4 at $4.11-1/2 a bushel.

Traders also said the wheat market was firm because the market is not expecting any wheat to be posted for delivery against the December contract. Friday, November 29 is first notice day for deliveries on CBOT December.
Bullish technical indicators included a bull-flag from the four and 20-day moving averages for the December through May contacts.
First resistance in the December was at $4.17 per bushel and second resistance was at $4.30-1/2. First support was at $4.03-1/2 and second support at $3.90.

The daily short-term nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for December was at 64.5 points as of 1150 CST and the 14-day RSI was at 58 points. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
The four-day moving average (MA) at 1153 CST was near $4.07, 18-day $3.88 and 40-day at $4.02.
